literature.headline_zh: 埃博拉病毒类群本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期埃博拉病毒类群研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 感染后,动物出现进行性临床疾病,表现为显著体重减轻和行为及外观的明显变化。尸检分析显示所有测试器官以及血清中均存在高病毒载量和病毒基因组拷贝数,这与病毒在全身广泛传播一致。组织病理学检查显示显著的病变,尤其是在肝脏和脾脏中。终末血清分析显示广泛的、显著的炎症反应,与非感染对照组相比,多种细胞因子和趋化因子浓度显著升高。 [10.1371/journal.pone.0347080]
对Inmazeb的结构建模显示,尽管Odesivimab保持表位结合,但Atoltivimab和Maftivimab单独无法结合其指定位点,但完整的三聚体鸡尾酒表现出对BDBV的协同结合。 [10.1038/s41467-026-78077-9]
该模型指出,人类活动,如自给自足狩猎和人口迁移,显著增加了跨物种溢出事件的风险,尤其是在冲突和粮食不安全影响的地区。 [10.1038/d44148-026-00296-5]
有共识认为,病毒特异性CD4+和CD8+ T细胞在自然或疫苗诱导的保护中的证据为VST开发提供了生物学基础。然而,这些证据并未确立过继转移VST的有效性。SARS-CoV-2提供了临床概念验证,表明部分HLA匹配或库存的病毒反应性T细胞产品可用于新出现的病原体。 [10.58460/jccma.v1i01.277]
截至2026年8月11日,刚果民主共和国的暴发报告了4,566例确诊病例和2,128例死亡病例,病例/死亡比率为46.6%。在之前的24小时内,报告了118例新确诊病例和67例死亡病例,这是暴发期间记录的最高单日确诊病例数。 [10.1038/s41591-026-04698-8]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Following infection, animals developed progressive clinical disease characterized by substantial weight loss and pronounced changes in behavior and appearance. [10.1371/journal.pone.0347080]

Structural modeling of Inmazeb shows that while Odesivimab maintains epitope binding, Atoltivimab and Maftivimab fail to bind their designated sites individually, though the complete trimeric cocktail demonstrates BDBV synergistic binding. [10.1038/s41467-026-78077-9]

The model identified that human activity, such as subsistence hunting and displacement, significantly increased the risk of spillover events, particularly in regions affected by conflict and food insecurity. [10.1038/d44148-026-00296-5]

There is consensus that evidence of natural or vaccine-induced protection by CD4+ and CD8+ T cells provides a biological basis for VST development. However, this evidence does not establish the efficacy of adoptively transferred VSTs. [10.58460/jccma.v1i01.277]

As of 11 August 2026, the DRC outbreak had reported 4,566 confirmed cases and 2,128 confirmed deaths, with a case/fatality ratio of 46.6%. During the preceding 24 hours, 118 new confirmed cases and 67 deaths were reported, representing the highest daily number of confirmed cases recorded during the outbreak. [10.1038/s41591-026-04698-8]

literature.en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments. Following infection, animals developed progressive clinical disease characterized by substantial weight loss and pronounced changes in behavior and appearance. [10.1371/journal.pone.0347080]. Structural modeling of Inmazeb shows that while Odesivimab maintains epitope binding, Atoltivimab and Maftivimab fail to bind their designated sites individually, though the complete trimeric cocktail demonstrates BDBV synergistic binding. news.headline_zh: 埃博拉病毒类群本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期埃博拉病毒类群新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 世界卫生组织(WHO)报告称由邦迪布古病毒引起的埃博拉病毒病暴发。该事件被确认为与邦迪布古病毒相关的埃博拉病毒病暴发。 [news-238ea7273ef38053]
截至2026年9月20日,刚果民主共和国(DRC)卫生部确认了邦迪布古 埃博拉病毒病 暴发,该事件已导致7,733例确诊病例、3,732例死亡和1,902例康复。该事件由IOM第19期情况报告报道。 [news-f960f99296c51550]
Hilleman实验室正在开发并生产用于临床试验的邦迪布古埃博拉病毒疫苗剂量,该工作得到了CEPI资金支持,并采用rVSV平台。 [news-d95816dbdf1fbcbf]
由邦迪布古病毒引起的埃博拉病毒病已在刚果民主共和国被报告,该暴发已扩展至包括两个新增卫生区。疫情被描述为持续发生,需要进一步调查以了解导致死亡率率升高的因素。 [news-f63c28a25052a2ec]
刚果民主共和国的邦迪布古约病毒病暴发进一步扩散,最新受影响地区为上乌埃尔省的Dungu卫生区。世界卫生组织(WHO)在第19周外部情况报告中报告了这一情况,数据截至2026年9月20日。该事件已确认,暴发仍是一个持续的公共卫生问题。 [news-5bd0c4072f656d46]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Ebola viruses news developments.
key_findings_en: Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus was reported by the World Health Organization (WHO). The event is confirmed as an outbreak of Ebola disease associated with the Bundibugyo virus. [news-238ea7273ef38053]

The Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease outbreak was confirmed by the Ministry of Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) as of 20 September 2026, with 7,733 confirmed cases, 3,732 deaths, and 1,902 recoveries. The event is reported by the IOM Situation Report No. [news-f960f99296c51550]
Hilleman Laboratories is developing and producing Bundibugyo ebolavirus vaccine doses for clinical trials, supported by CEPI funding and using the rVSV platform. [news-d95816dbdf1fbcbf]

Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus has been reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with the outbreak expanding to include two additional health zones. The situation is described as ongoing and requires further investigation to understand factors contributing to the elevated mortality rate. [news-f63c28a25052a2ec]

The Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has expanded further, with Dungu Health Zone in Haut-Uélé Province being the latest affected area. This is reported by the World Health Organization (WHO) in the Weekly External Situation Report 19, as of 20 September 2026. [news-5bd0c4072f656d46]

papers.title: Lethal Sudan virus infection in IFNAR-/- mice is characterized by key inflammatory features of filovirus disease
papers.abstract: Sudan virus (SUDV) is a member of the family Filoviridae , which comprises highly pathogenic viruses associated with unusually high case fatality rates. The development of medical countermeasures against filoviruses, including antivirals, vaccines, and therapeutic antibodies, requires preclinical evaluation in suitable animal models. C57BL/6J IFNAR -/- mice, which lack the type I interferon (IFN-α/β) receptor, have been reported to be susceptible to filovirus infections, although their impaired innate immune response may represent a potential limitation of the model. Here, we characterized the clinical, virological, pathological, and inflammatory responses following SUDV Boniface infection in IFNAR -/- mice. Following infection, animals developed progressive clinical disease characterized by substantial weight loss and pronounced changes in behavior and appearance. Mice reached the predefined clinical endpoint 3–5 days post infection. Post mortem analysis of terminal samples revealed high viral loads and viral genome copies in all tested organs as well as in serum, consistent with widespread systemic dissemination. Histopathological examination revealed prominent lesions, particularly in the liver and spleen. In addition, terminal serum analysis revealed a broad and pronounced inflammatory response, with significantly elevated concentrations of multiple cytokines and chemokines compared with non-infected controls, encompassing pro-inflammatory, regulatory, and hematopoietic mediators. Together, these findings characterize the clinical course, systemic viral dissemination, tissue pathology, and terminal inflammatory response associated with lethal SUDV infection in IFNAR -/- mice. The observed cytokine and chemokine elevations are consistent with inflammatory responses described in filovirus infections, although the single terminal sampling time point and limited cohort size preclude conclusions regarding the temporal development or mechanistic basis of this response. These data support the utility of this model for investigating filovirus pathogenesis and infection-associated immune responses and warrant further evaluation of its suitability for SUDV infection and for preclinical studies of filovirus countermeasures.

C57BL/6J IFNAR -/- mice, which lack the type I interferon (IFN-α/β) receptor, have been reported to be susceptible to filovirus infections, although their impaired innate immune response may represent a potential limitation of the model. Here, we characterized the clinical, virological, pathological, and inflammatory responses following SUDV Boniface infection in IFNAR -/- mice. Following infection, animals developed progressive clinical disease characterized by substantial weight loss and pronounced changes in behavior and appearance. Mice reached the predefined clinical endpoint 3–5 days post infection. Post mortem analysis of terminal samples revealed high viral loads and viral genome copies in all tested organs as well as in serum, consistent with widespread systemic dissemination. Histopathological examination revealed prominent lesions, particularly in the liver and spleen. In addition, terminal serum analysis revealed a broad and pronounced inflammatory response, with significantly elevated concentrations of multiple cytokines and chemokines compared with non-infected controls, encompassing pro-inflammatory, regulatory, and hematopoietic mediators. Together, these findings characterize the clinical course, systemic viral dissemination, tissue pathology, and terminal inflammatory response associated with lethal SUDV infection in IFNAR -/- mice. The observed cytokine and chemokine elevations are consistent with inflammatory responses described in filovirus infections, although the single terminal sampling time point and limited cohort size preclude conclusions regarding the temporal development or mechanistic basis of this response. These data support the utility of this model for investigating filovirus pathogenesis and infection-associated immune responses and warrant further evaluation of its suitability for SUDV infection and for preclinical studies of filovirus countermeasures.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 苏丹病毒(SUDV)是丝状病毒科(Filoviridae)的成员,该科包含与异常高病死率相关的高度致病性病毒。针对丝状病毒的医疗对策(包括抗病毒药物、疫苗和治疗性抗体)的开发需要在合适的动物模型中进行临床前评估。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究描述了C57BL/6J IFNAR-/-小鼠在苏丹病毒Boniface株感染后的临床、病毒学、病理学和炎症反应,这些小鼠缺乏I型干扰素(IFN-α/β)受体,并已被报道对丝状病毒感染易感。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究使用C57BL/6J IFNAR-/-小鼠,并通过临床、病毒学、病理学和炎症分析描述了苏丹病毒Boniface株感染后的反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 感染后,动物出现进行性临床疾病,表现为显著体重减轻和行为及外观的明显变化。尸检分析显示所有测试器官以及血清中均存在高病毒载量和病毒基因组拷贝数,这与病毒在全身广泛传播一致。组织病理学检查显示显著的病变,尤其是在肝脏和脾脏中。终末血清分析显示广泛的、显著的炎症反应,与非感染对照组相比,多种细胞因子和趋化因子浓度显著升高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些数据支持该模型用于研究丝状病毒发病机制和感染相关免疫应答的实用性,并需要进一步评估其在SUDV感染和丝状病毒对策临床前研究中的适用性。观察到的细胞因子和趋化因子浓度升高与丝状病毒感染中描述的炎症反应一致,但单一终末采样时间点和有限的队列研究样本量限制了对这种反应的时间发展或机制基础的结论。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现描述了IFNAR-/-小鼠中致命性SUDV感染的临床过程、全身病毒传播、组织病理学变化和终末炎症反应,这些信息可以用于监测、诊断、治疗以及未来对SUDV和其他丝状病毒的研究。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 单一终末采样时间点和有限的队列研究样本量限制了对炎症反应的时间发展或机制基础的结论。数据表明该模型在研究丝状病毒发病机制和感染相关免疫应答方面具有一定的实用性,但仍需进一步评估。

papers.title: Early insights into predicted efficacy of Ebola monoclonal antibodies for the 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak
papers.abstract: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the DRC and Uganda raises urgent questions about the efficacy of existing Ebola virus (EBOV) monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). Here, we perform genomic and structural analyses of 44 BDBV sequences, including 12 from the 2026 outbreak, to assess mAb binding to the viral glycoprotein (GP). While the MBP134 cocktail epitopes remain conserved, mAb114 (Ebanga) binding is compromised by E112D and P116A mutations, causing off-target binding and reduced affinity. Structural modeling of Inmazeb shows that while Odesivimab maintains epitope binding, Atoltivimab and Maftivimab fail to bind their designated sites individually, though the complete trimeric cocktail demonstrates BDBV synergistic binding. These computational models predict mAb114 efficacy against BDBV may be compromised due to epitope mutations affecting binding affinity, whereas MBP134 retains conserved targeting and holds promise as a broadly protective therapeutic. The complex binding behavior of Inmazeb components points to the importance of antibody combinatorial effects for treatment efficacy. These observations warrant urgent experimental validation through neutralization assays. Rapid predictive methods narrow the solution space in an outbreak setting. In this computational study, the authors find that cocktail treatments for Ebola Zaire could be more effective than monotherapies against the 2026 Bundibugyo strain.

papers.title_zh: 2026年刚果民主共和国和乌干达邦迪布古病毒病早期对预测单克隆抗体疗效的见解暴发
papers.source_body_en: The 2026 Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) outbreak in the DRC and Uganda raises urgent questions about the efficacy of existing Ebola virus (EBOV) monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). Here, we perform genomic and structural analyses of 44 BDBV sequences, including 12 from the 2026 outbreak, to assess mAb binding to the viral glycoprotein (GP). While the MBP134 cocktail epitopes remain conserved, mAb114 (Ebanga) binding is compromised by E112D and P116A mutations, causing off-target binding and reduced affinity. Structural modeling of Inmazeb shows that while Odesivimab maintains epitope binding, Atoltivimab and Maftivimab fail to bind their designated sites individually, though the complete trimeric cocktail demonstrates BDBV synergistic binding. These computational models predict mAb114 efficacy against BDBV may be compromised due to epitope mutations affecting binding affinity, whereas MBP134 retains conserved targeting and holds promise as a broadly protective therapeutic. The complex binding behavior of Inmazeb components points to the importance of antibody combinatorial effects for treatment efficacy. These observations warrant urgent experimental validation through neutralization assays. Rapid predictive methods narrow the solution space in an outbreak setting. In this computational study, the authors find that cocktail treatments for Ebola Zaire could be more effective than monotherapies against the 2026 Bundibugyo strain.
papers.abstract_zh: 2026年刚果民主共和国和乌干达邦迪布古病毒病(BVD)暴发引发了对现有埃博拉病毒(EBOV)单克隆抗体(mAbs)针对邦迪布古病毒(BDBV)疗效的迫切问题。在此,我们对44个BDBV序列(包括12个来自2026年暴发的序列)进行了基因组和结构分析,以评估mAb对病毒糖蛋白(GP)的结合情况。尽管MBP134鸡尾酒的表位保持保守,但mAb114(Ebanga)的结合受到E112D和P116A 突变的影响,导致脱靶结合和亲和力降低。对Inmazeb的结构建模显示,尽管Odesivimab保持表位结合,但Atoltivimab和Maftivimab单独无法结合其指定位点,但完整的三聚体鸡尾酒表现出对BDBV的协同结合。这些计算模型预测,由于表位突变影响结合亲和力,mAb114对BDBV的疗效可能受到损害,而MBP134保留了保守的靶向性,并有望作为广泛保护的治疗药物。Inmazeb组分的复杂结合行为表明,抗体组合效应对于治疗疗效至关重要。这些观察结果需要通过中和试验进行紧急实验验证。快速预测方法在暴发环境下缩小了解决方案空间。在这项计算研究中,作者发现针对埃博拉扎伊尔毒株的鸡尾酒治疗可能比单药治疗对2026年邦迪布古毒株更有效。

papers.full_text: Volume 32, Number 10—October 2026 Synopsis Early Action Review of Detection, Notification, and Response Timeliness during Cross-Border Bundibugyo Virus Disease Outbreak, Uganda, 2026 Cite This Article Citation for Media Abstract Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), an Ebola virus species with no licensed vaccine or therapeutic, reemerged in May 2026 as a cross-border outbreak in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. During a 2-day workshop, July 8–9, 2026, we conducted an early action review of the outbreak response using the 7-1-7 framework (7 days to detect, 1 day to notify, 7 days to complete early response actions) to assess timeliness and identify bottlenecks and enablers across 9 response pillars. Uganda declared its outbreak on May 15, 2026; by July 8, the country had recorded 20 confirmed cases (15 imported, 5 locally transmitted) and a case-fatality rate of 15%. Uganda met all 3 targets: detection in 6 days, notification in <1 day, and response completion in 2 days. Low clinical suspicion, cross-border data-sharing gaps, fragmented digital systems, and delayed community engagement were common bottlenecks; strong leadership and coordination structures were most cited enablers. Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD) is a severe viral hemorrhagic fever caused by Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense, a documented Ebola virus species. The virus was first identified during a 2007 outbreak in Bundibugyo District, western Uganda (1); that outbreak ultimately comprised 131 cases, including 56 laboratory-confirmed cases and a case-fatality rate (CFR) of 40% among confirmed cases (2–4). Bundibugyo virus subsequently caused a second confirmed outbreak, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in 2012, comprising 62 cases, including 36 laboratory-confirmed cases and a CFR of 33% among confirmed cases (5). Reported CFRs for BVD are generally lower than for Ebola caused by Zaire ebolavirus (6). Unlike other Ebola virus species, no licensed vaccine or approved specific therapeutic currently exists for BVD, although licensed Zaire ebolavirus vaccines show early evidence of partial cross-reactive immunogenicity, and candidate BVD-specific vaccines and therapeutics are undergoing World Health Organization (WHO)–led prioritization (7–11). On May 15, 2026, both Uganda and the DRC declared separate outbreaks, a transboundary BVD event, from which cases were epidemiologically linked to Ituri Province, DRC (12). Uganda’s index case, a 59-year-old DRC national, sought care at a private hospital in Kampala on May 11, 2026, and died on May 14, 2026 (13). On May 17, 2026, WHO determined the event constituted a Public Health Emergency of International Concern under the International Health Regulations 2005 (14), and on May 18, 2026, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (15). By July 8, 2026, Uganda had recorded 20 confirmed cases, of which 15 were directly imported from the DRC, underscoring the cross-border nature of the outbreak and the need for sustained joint surveillance and coordinated screening along the Uganda–DRC corridor. The 7-1-7 target, defined as <7 days to detect a suspected outbreak, <1 day to notify relevant public health authorities, and <7 days to complete essential early response actions, was jointly developed by WHO and Resolve to Save Lives, a nongovernmental global public health organization (16). The 7-1-7 target has been adopted by dozens of countries and institutions worldwide as a standardized, real-world performance benchmark for outbreak detection and response (16,17). Retrospective, multicountry evidence indicates substantial variation in how consistently those targets are met in practice (18,19), and Uganda has since institutionalized 7-1-7 monitoring as part of its national outbreak coordination platform (20); subsequent applications have been documented across other outbreak types in the country (21). WHO recommends that an early action review (EAR), an agile, structured methodology for assessing timeliness and identifying bottlenecks and enablers using the 7-1-7 tool, be conducted for all outbreaks of public health significance (22). The EAR formally assesses the timeliness of detection, notification, and response against the 7-1-7 targets, while enabling countries to evaluate coordination effectiveness within and across response pillars, identify pillar-level bottlenecks and enablers, and document emerging good practices. Uganda conducted its EAR ≈8 weeks into the BVD response, as both an operational necessity and a formal obligation under the International Health Regulations 2005 Monitoring and Evaluation Framework (23). The process further assisted with development of actionable, time-bound recommendations to strengthen the ongoing response and inform national preparedness and readiness planning, in line with Uganda’s National Action Plan for Health Security (NAPHS), 2024–2029. In this article, we present the process, results, and lessons learned from that review. Study Design and Setting We conducted a retrospective, multipillar programmatic review using WHO’s standardized EAR methodology and 7-1-7 assessment tool (22). Nine response pillars were scoped for review under Uganda’s incident management system (IMS) structure: coordination; surveillance; laboratory; case management; risk communication and community engagement (RCCE); water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH); logistics; strategic information, research, and innovation (SIRI); and continuity of essential health services (CEHS). We convened a 2-day workshop during July 8–9, 2026, bringing together participants from the Uganda Ministry of Health (MoH) and implementing and development partners, as well as experts from WHO, Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, and the UK Health Security Agency. The 7-1-7 Framework The 7-1-7 tool defines 3 sequential intervals: detection, the interval from the date of disease emergence (here defined as the earliest date on which a confirmed BVD case crossed the border into Uganda, thereby introducing the risk) to the date the event was first recorded by any source, against a target of <7 days; notification, the interval from the date of detection to formal notification of the public health authority responsible for action, against a target of <1 day; and response, the interval from notification to completion of the last of 7 defined early response actions (investigation, epidemiologic and risk assessment, laboratory confirmation, case management and infection prevention and control (IPC) measures, public health countermeasures, risk communication, and establishment of a coordination mechanism) against a target of <7 days (16,17). Data Collection and Synthesis A total of 74 participants—38 from MoH, 12 from development, and 24 implementing partners—convened in 9 IMS pillar-based breakout groups, each supported by a trained facilitator and note-taker. Using the 7-1-7 standardized tool, each group reconstructed its pillar’s timeliness of detection, notification, and response actions; calculated interval timeliness against target; identified bottlenecks and enablers; and proposed immediate and longer-term remedial actions. On the second day, pillar findings were presented and discussed in plenary, enabling cross-pillar validation, consensus-building, and refinement of the consolidated bottlenecks, enablers, and recommendations. We subsequently consolidated findings centrally across all 9 pillars, and tagged each item to its source pillar for traceability. Ethics Considerations This review constituted a programmatic evaluation of routine public health outbreak response activities using non–patient-identifiable process data. It was conducted under the MoH’s standing mandate for outbreak response and quality improvement and did not constitute human subjects research requiring separate ethical review. Outbreak Overview By July 8, 2026, Uganda had confirmed 20 BVD cases: 15 imported from the DRC and 5 arising from secondary transmission within the country. The CFR stood at 15% among confirmed cases. Of the 831 contacts identified by then, 6 seroconverted, 4 died of causes unrelated to BVD, 1 was repatriated to DRC on request, and the remainder completed the standard 21-day follow-up according to existing guidelines. The country had tested >2,337 persons from 106 districts who were suspected of having any viral hemorrhagic fever (VHF), including samples from mortality surveillance. Case accrual slowed markedly as the response advanced. Uganda’s confirmed case count rose only marginally, from 19 cases as of June 17, 2026, to 20 by July 8, 2026, consistent with effective containment of secondary transmission following the initial response. 7-1-7 Timeliness We summarized interval timeliness of the BVD response against the 7-1-7 targets (Table 1). Uganda’s earliest cross-border BVD case was traced to May 8, 2026 (date of emergence). The event was first recorded by the health system on May 14, 2026, when a community leader alerted the Director General of Health Services, giving a detection interval of 6 days (target <7 days). Formal notification occurred the same day, a notification interval of <1 day (target <1). The last of the 7 early response actions was completed on May 16, 2026, two days after notification (target <7). Uganda therefore met all 3 of the 7-1-7 targets for this event. Enablers by Pillar We consolidated the enablers identified across all 9 pillar breakout groups, organized by pillar (Table 2). Three cross-pillar enablers were consistently cited: presence of strong senior leadership, reinforced by existing coordination architecture such as the National Task Force, the IMS, and the National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre, underpinning rapid activation across nearly every pillar; Uganda’s past experience in managing similar outbreaks, coupled with existing digital systems; and a trained, well-experienced, and ready-to-deploy workforce. Bottlenecks and Action Matrix–Proposed Immediate and Longer-Term Recommendations We compiled a list of bottlenecks identified for each pillar (Table 3). Two major cross-cutting patterns emerged. First, a low index of clinical suspicion, attributable to the nonclassical, symptom-predominant manifestations of the BVD strain rather than the classic hemorrhagic symptoms (24), recurred as a root cause in both the surveillance and case management pillars. Those bottlenecks contributed to delayed recognition, referral, and IPC uptake, especially in private healthcare facilities. Second, fragmentation of digital and information systems recurred across the surveillance, logistics, and SIRI pillars, manifesting as parallel electronic information systems, limited real-time stock visibility, and poor interoperability between reporting platforms. For each bottleneck identified during the review, the corresponding pillar group proposed a remedial action, distinguishing actions for immediate implementation from actions requiring longer-term planning and funding, for example, through the NAPHS (2024–2029) or partner-funded programs (Table 3). All actions were validated in plenary on the second day of the workshop and discussed critically for feasibility and ownership by the respective pillar group. This EAR found that Uganda met all 3 of the 7-1-7 targets during the 2026 cross-border BVD outbreak: detection achieved within 6 days, notification within 1 day, and completion of early response actions within 2 days. Meeting all 3 of the 7-1-7 targets simultaneously is an excellent finding in practice; a 5-country retrospective assessment of 41 public health events found that only 54% of events met the detection targets, 71% the notification targets, and 49% the response targets (18). Our results are thus consistent with Uganda’s early gains reported from its national 7-1-7 rollout (20,21). Similar EARs conducted for a cholera outbreak in Kenya (N. Roosevelt et al., unpub. data, https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.07.29.25332335) and a measles outbreak in Sierra Leone (25) have also identified actionable, pillar-specific bottlenecks, suggesting that the EAR methodology yields consistently useful operational insight across pathogens and settings. The low proportion of cases attributable to secondary transmission (5 of 20) further suggests that timeliness translated into a real reduction in onward transmission of a pathogen for which no licensed vaccine or therapeutic currently exists (7). Despite the strong aggregate timeliness of the early BVD response, the review identified concrete opportunities for improvement. Generally, the ongoing transboundary BVD outbreak has illustrated the persistent clinical and public health challenges posed by filovirus disease outbreaks in resource-limited settings, including diagnostic delay and the demands of a coordinated field response (26). The recurrence of low clinical suspicion across both the surveillance and case management pillars is a notable finding; the clinical manifestation of cases in this outbreak was characterized predominantly by fever and gastrointestinal symptoms, rather than overt hemorrhage (24). Therefore, frontline health workers trained on a classic hemorrhagic case definition might have underrecognized the disease clinically, delaying isolation, IPC measures, and referral, particularly in private healthcare facilities. That initial gap in suspicion was rapidly narrowed by public awareness campaigns, intensified contact tracing, mortality surveillance, and point of entry (PoE) screening. We attribute the limited secondary transmission (5 of 20 cases) chiefly to those fast-follow interventions, rather than to missed cases during the outbreak’s earliest, low-suspicion phase. That finding further suggests that case definition training and job aids should explicitly incorporate the nonhemorrhagic manifestation of BVD as documented in this outbreak, rather than relying solely on generic Ebola virus disease case definitions. Similarly, the recurrence of digital and information-system fragmentation across the surveillance, laboratory, logistics, and SIRI pillars, including suboptimal electronic laboratory information system use, limited stock visibility, and poor system interoperability, points to a structural rather than pillar-specific weakness in Uganda’s outbreak information architecture. Such shortfalls are likely to recur in future events unless they are addressed at the systems level, rather than pillar by pillar. The cross-border nature of this outbreak also foregrounded the need for real-time information-sharing with the DRC. Limited cross-border surveillance data-sharing was cited as a bottleneck despite the outbreak’s clear epidemiologic linkage to the parallel event in Ituri Province, DRC (12). That finding is further underscored by the fact that 15 of Uganda’s 20 confirmed cases were directly imported from the DRC, principally among persons in search of specialized medical care. Strengthening routine institutionalized cross-border collaboration, joint investigations, harmonized PoE screening, and regular bilateral coordination meetings were accordingly among the most frequently proposed immediate actions (Table 3), consistent with prior calls for stronger DRC–Uganda border health cooperation, given the recurring risk of spillover along this corridor (19). Such bidirectional dependence also means a well-prepared country can strengthen its neighbor’s early warning. Uganda’s own detection benefited from informal advanced notice of suspected Ituri Province cases, and the country has since extended preparedness support to healthcare facilities along the shared corridor. The strong response-interval performance we identified also reflects a third cross-cutting pattern (Table 2): decisive senior leadership operating through existing coordination architecture. An incident commander was appointed within 3 hours of the initial case confirmation, and the National Task Force, IMS, and National Public Health Emergency Operations Centre were activated immediately, consistent with WHO’s requirement that a public health emergency operations center be fully activated within 120 minutes of detecting any public health event (27). The MoH was also able to make a public declaration of the event within the same day that the laboratory confirmed the index case. Of note, however, the coordination pillar’s own submission also reported a bottleneck of the opposite character: continued partner implementation of some response activities outside pillar coordination structures, leading to inconsistent response coordination. That finding indicates that strong central leadership did not, by itself, guarantee full coordination of all actors at the response start phase and that institutionalizing the coordination structures themselves, rather than relying on the persons who led this particular response, warrants continued attention (28). Many of the enablers we identified reflect capacities built over nearly 2 decades of response to recurrent filovirus outbreaks in Uganda, including the 2007 BDV event (2–4). Those events catalyzed sustained investment in ready-to-deploy rapid response teams, national and regional public health emergency operations centers, mobile laboratory capacity, prepositioned emergency stocks, and predeveloped risk communication materials, among other capacities. Countries lacking such infrastructure might need to apply a narrower subset of the enablers to achieve comparable 7-1-7 performance. Beyond the specific bottlenecks discussed above, the pillar-generated action matrix (Table 3) warrants critical comment on implementation feasibility. Surveillance alone accounts for 5 of the 17 immediate actions, raising a practical question about parallel implementation capacity within an already-stretched pillar team. papers.title_original: Early Action Review of Detection, Notification, and Response Timeliness during Cross-Border Bundibugyo Virus Disease Outbreak, Uganda, 2026

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the detection, notification, and response timeliness during a cross-border Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2026. The central question is how effectively the 7-1-7 framework was applied to assess outbreak response performance and identify bottlenecks and enablers.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review was conducted using a 2-day workshop in July 2026, employing the 7-1-7 framework to evaluate outbreak response timeliness. The framework includes 7 days to detect, 1 day to notify, and 7 days to complete essential early response actions. The review included data from 9 response pillars and was based on retrospective, multicountry evidence.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Uganda met all three 7-1-7 targets: detection in 6 days, notification in <1 day, and response completion in 2 days. The review identified low clinical suspicion, cross-border data-sharing gaps, fragmented digital systems, and delayed community engagement as common bottlenecks, while strong leadership and coordination structures were cited as key enablers.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is evidence of substantial variation in how consistently the 7-1-7 targets are met in practice across different countries and institutions. Additionally, the review highlights the need for sustained joint surveillance and coordinated screening along the Uganda–DRC corridor due to the cross-border nature of the outbreak.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: WHO recommends conducting early action reviews (EAR) for all outbreaks of public health significance. The review emphasizes the importance of improving clinical suspicion, enhancing cross-border data-sharing, and strengthening digital systems to ensure timely detection and response. It also underscores the need for further research into BVD-specific vaccines and therapeutics.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the detection, notification, and response timeliness during a cross-border Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2026. Using the 7-1-7 framework, the review found that Uganda met all three targets: detection in 6 days, notification in <1 day, and response completion in 2 days. Common bottlenecks included low clinical suspicion, fragmented digital systems, and delayed community engagement, while strong leadership and coordination were key enablers. The review highlights the need for improved cross-border surveillance and the development of BVD-specific vaccines and therapeutics. WHO recommends early action reviews for all public health outbreaks to identify and address response challenges effectively.

elements_en.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the detection, notification, and response timeliness during a cross-border Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2026. The central question is how effectively the 7-1-7 framework was applied to assess outbreak response performance and identify bottlenecks and enablers.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review was conducted using a 2-day workshop in July 2026, employing the 7-1-7 framework to evaluate outbreak response timeliness. The framework includes 7 days to detect, 1 day to notify, and 7 days to complete essential early response actions. The review included data from 9 response pillars and was based on retrospective, multicountry evidence.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Uganda met all three 7-1-7 targets: detection in 6 days, notification in <1 day, and response completion in 2 days. The review identified low clinical suspicion, cross-border data-sharing gaps, fragmented digital systems, and delayed community engagement as common bottlenecks, while strong leadership and coordination structures were cited as key enablers.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: There is evidence of substantial variation in how consistently the 7-1-7 targets are met in practice across different countries and institutions. Additionally, the review highlights the need for sustained joint surveillance and coordinated screening along the Uganda–DRC corridor due to the cross-border nature of the outbreak.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: WHO recommends conducting early action reviews (EAR) for all outbreaks of public health significance. The review emphasizes the importance of improving clinical suspicion, enhancing cross-border data-sharing, and strengthening digital systems to ensure timely detection and response. It also underscores the need for further research into BVD-specific vaccines and therapeutics.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本审查聚焦于2026年乌干达和刚果民主共和国跨境邦迪布古病毒病暴发期间的检测、通报和响应及时性。核心问题是:如何有效地应用7-1-7框架来评估暴发响应表现,并识别瓶颈和促进因素。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 此次审查于2026年7月通过为期2天的工作坊进行,采用7-1-7框架评估暴发响应的及时性。该框架包括7天用于检测,1天用于通知,以及7天用于完成必要的早期响应行动。审查涵盖了9个响应支柱的数据,并基于回顾性、多国的证据。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 乌干达达到了所有三个7-1-7目标:在6天内完成检测、在不到1天内完成通报、在2天内完成响应行动。审查发现,低临床怀疑、跨境数据共享的不足、数字系统的碎片化以及社区参与的延迟是常见的瓶颈,而强有力的领导和协调结构则被广泛认为是关键的促进因素。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 有证据表明,不同国家和机构在实际操作中对7-1-7目标的达成存在显著差异。此外,审查还强调了由于该暴发的跨境性质,需要在乌干达-刚果民主共和国走廊上持续进行联合监测和协调筛查。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 世界卫生组织(WHO)建议,对所有具有公共卫生意义的暴发开展早期行动审查(EAR)。审查强调了提高临床怀疑、增强跨境数据共享以及加强数字系统的重要性,以确保及时的检测和响应。同时,它还突出了进一步研究BVD特异性疫苗和治疗药物的必要性。

papers.title_zh: 跨境本迪布焦病毒病 暴发 期间检测、通知和响应及时性的早期行动审查,乌干达,2026 年
papers.source_body_en: Volume 32, Number 10—October 2026 Synopsis Early Action Review of Detection, Notification, and Response Timeliness during Cross-Border Bundibugyo Virus Disease Outbreak, Uganda, 2026 Cite This Article Citation for Media Abstract Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), an Ebola virus species with no licensed vaccine or therapeutic, reemerged in May 2026 as a cross-border outbreak in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. During a 2-day workshop, July 8–9, 2026, we conducted an early action review of the outbreak response using the 7-1-7 framework (7 days to detect, 1 day to notify, 7 days to complete early response actions) to assess timeliness and identify bottlenecks and enablers across 9 response pillars. WHO recommends that an early action review (EAR), an agile, structured methodology for assessing timeliness and identifying bottlenecks and enablers using the 7-1-7 tool, be conducted for all outbreaks of public health significance (22). In this article, we present the process, results, and lessons learned from that review. Study Design and Setting We conducted a retrospective, multipillar programmatic review using WHO’s standardized EAR methodology and 7-1-7 assessment tool (22). Uganda declared its outbreak on May 15, 2026; by July 8, the country had recorded 20 confirmed cases (15 imported, 5 locally transmitted) and a case-fatality rate of 15%. Uganda met all 3 targets: detection in 6 days, notification in <1 day, and response completion in 2 days. Low clinical suspicion, cross-border data-sharing gaps, fragmented digital systems, and delayed community engagement were common bottlenecks; strong leadership and coordination structures were most cited enablers. analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本审查聚焦于2026年乌干达和刚果民主共和国跨境邦迪布古病毒病暴发期间的检测、通报和响应及时性。核心问题是:如何有效地应用7-1-7框架来评估暴发响应表现,并识别瓶颈和促进因素。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 此次审查于2026年7月通过为期2天的工作坊进行,采用7-1-7框架评估暴发响应的及时性。该框架包括7天用于检测,1天用于通知,以及7天用于完成必要的早期响应行动。审查涵盖了9个响应支柱的数据,并基于回顾性、多国的证据。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 乌干达达到了所有三个7-1-7目标:在6天内完成检测、在不到1天内完成通报、在2天内完成响应行动。审查发现,低临床怀疑、跨境数据共享的不足、数字系统的碎片化以及社区参与的延迟是常见的瓶颈,而强有力的领导和协调结构则被广泛认为是关键的促进因素。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 有证据表明,不同国家和机构在实际操作中对7-1-7目标的达成存在显著差异。此外,审查还强调了由于该暴发的跨境性质,需要在乌干达-刚果民主共和国走廊上持续进行联合监测和协调筛查。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 世界卫生组织(WHO)建议,对所有具有公共卫生意义的暴发开展早期行动审查(EAR)。审查强调了提高临床怀疑、增强跨境数据共享以及加强数字系统的重要性,以确保及时的检测和响应。同时,它还突出了进一步研究BVD特异性疫苗和治疗药物的必要性。

papers.title: Harnessing Coordinated CD4+ and CD8+ T-Cell Immunity for Virus-Specific Adoptive Immunotherapy in Africa
papers.abstract: Virus-specific T-cell (VST) therapy has developed principally for persistent or reactivating viral infections in immunocompromised patients, with the strongest clinical experience involving cytomegalovirus, Epstein–Barr virus, human adenovirus, BK polyomavirus and human herpesvirus 6. Whether this approach can be extended to emerging and re-emerging viral infections remains less certain. Evidence that virus-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T cells contribute to natural or vaccine-induced protection provides a biological basis for therapeutic development but does not establish the efficacy of adoptively transferred VSTs. This distinction is particularly important for viruses of relevance to Africa, including Ebola virus, Lassa virus, Marburg virus, dengue virus, chikungunya virus, Rift Valley fever virus and mpox virus. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) provides clinical proof-of-concept that rapidly developed, partially HLA-matched or banked virus-reactive T-cell products can be administered against a newly emerging pathogen. Experimental adoptive transfer studies provide additional evidence for selected pathogens, including Ebola virus, whereas other emerging viruses remain supported mainly by human immunological, epitope or preclinical data. Translation to African populations will require definition of protective viral targets, population-relevant HLA restrictions, viral sequence conservation, manufacturing feasibility and clinical indications in which cellular therapy offers a clear advantage. This review examines the evidence required to move from antiviral T-cell immunity to therapeutic VST development and proposes a framework for evaluating emerging and re-emerging viral infections as future VST targets in Africa.
papers.journal: Journal of Clinical Care and Medical Advancement

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on the development of virus-specific T-cell (VST) therapy for human-pathogenic orthoebolaviruses and Ebola virus disease. The central question is whether VST therapy can be extended to emerging and re-emerging viral infections relevant to Africa, including Ebola virus, Sudan virus, Bundibugyo virus, Taï Forest virus, and Zaire ebolavirus.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic analysis of the evidence required to transition from understanding antiviral T-cell immunity to developing therapeutic VSTs. It includes experimental adoptive transfer studies, human immunological data, epitope information, and preclinical findings for selected pathogens, with a focus on Ebola virus and other related viruses. The review does not report specific databases, search dates, or study counts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: There is consensus that evidence of natural or vaccine-induced protection by CD4+ and CD8+ T cells provides a biological basis for VST development. However, this evidence does not establish the efficacy of adoptively transferred VSTs. SARS-CoV-2 offers clinical proof-of-concept that partially HLA-matched or banked virus-reactive T-cell products can be used against newly emerging pathogens.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The efficacy of adoptively transferred VSTs for emerging and re-emerging viruses, including Ebola virus, remains uncertain. While experimental studies provide evidence for some pathogens like Ebola virus, other emerging viruses are supported mainly by human immunological, epitope, or preclinical data. There is a lack of clear evidence on the population-relevant HLA restrictions, viral sequence conservation, and clinical indications where cellular therapy offers a clear advantage.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Further research is needed to define protective viral targets, population-relevant HLA restrictions, viral sequence conservation, and clinical indications for VST therapy in African populations. The review proposes a framework for evaluating emerging and re-emerging viral infections as potential VST targets, emphasizing the need for target-specific methods and results.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the potential of virus-specific T-cell (VST) therapy for treating Ebola virus and related pathogens in Africa. It highlights the biological basis for VST development through evidence of natural or vaccine-induced protection by CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, but notes that this does not confirm therapeutic efficacy. The review emphasizes the need for target-specific evidence, particularly for defining protective viral targets, HLA restrictions, and clinical applications. While SARS-CoV-2 provides a proof-of-concept for rapid VST development, other viruses like Ebola virus require more experimental and clinical data. The review proposes a framework for evaluating future VST targets, focusing on African populations and their unique health challenges.

papers.abstract_zh: 病毒特异性T细胞(VST)疗法主要针对免疫功能低下患者的持续性或复发性病毒感染,其中在临床经验方面最为丰富的包括巨细胞病毒、EB病毒、人类腺病毒、BK多瘤病毒和人类疱疹病毒6。这种方法是否可以扩展到新兴和再流行的病毒感染仍存在不确定性。有证据表明,病毒特异性CD4+和CD8+ T细胞在自然或疫苗诱导的保护中起作用,这为治疗性VST的开发提供了生物学基础,但并未确立过继转移VST的有效性。这一区别对于非洲相关病毒尤为重要,包括埃博拉病毒、拉沙病毒、马尔堡病毒、登革病毒、基孔肯雅病毒、裂谷热病毒和猴痘病毒。严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)提供了临床概念验证,表明可以快速开发、部分HLA匹配或库存的病毒反应性T细胞产品可用于新出现的病原体。实验性过继转移研究为某些病原体,如埃博拉病毒,提供了额外的证据,而其他新兴病毒则主要依赖于人类免疫学、表位或临床前数据。将该疗法应用于非洲人群需要定义保护性病毒靶标、人群相关的HLA限制、病毒序列保守性、制造可行性以及细胞治疗具有明显优势的临床指征。本综述探讨了从抗病毒药物 T细胞免疫到治疗性VST开发所需的证据,并提出了一个评估新兴和再流行病毒作为未来VST靶标的框架。

analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 需要进一步研究以定义VST疗法在非洲人群中的保护性病毒靶标、人群相关的HLA限制、病毒序列保守性以及细胞治疗具有明显优势的临床指征。综述提出了一个评估新兴和再流行病毒感染作为潜在VST靶标的框架,强调了针对特定靶标的方法和结果的重要性。}}.{

papers.full_text: Once an orthoebolavirus passes from an animal into a human, and transmission takes hold within a community, an outbreak can be extremely difficult to contain. The 2026 outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) brought renewed urgency to efforts to identify where spillovers may occur. Ebola outbreaks are recurring, with events recorded in 25 of the 50 years since the disease was first identified in 1976. As a result, a lot of effort has gone into trying to predict where the next spillover event could be, in the hope that it can aid efforts to check the disease in its tracks. These spillover events occur when the orthoebolaviruses – the group of viruses responsible for Ebola disease – take the cross-species or zoonotic leap from animals to humans. Researchers have developed a range of mathematical, statistical and ecological models to assess where Ebola spillover may be more likely.1 Many are habitat suitability models, which use factors such as temperature, rainfall and land cover to identify places where environmental conditions could support the viruses or their possible animal hosts. But habitat is only part of the picture. The 2026 outbreak emerged in a region affected by conflict, food insecurity and large-scale displacement. People escaping violence may have little choice but to depend more heavily on forests for food and income, including through subsistence hunting and artisanal mining. These pressures can bring communities into closer contact with wildlife and disturbed habitats. Monika Moir, a researcher at the Centre for Epidemic Response and Innovation at Stellenbosch University in South Africa, and her colleagues from the DRC, UK and US wanted to know whether a model that incorporated human activity could provide a clearer picture of where orthoebolavirus spillover may occur. Their preprint, Integrating ecological and anthropogenic risk identifies emerging Ebola spillover hotspots,2 brings together environmental and sociodemographic factors associated with previous spillover events. The international team included researchers from South Africa, the DRC, the United Kingdom and the United States. When ecology is not enough Four orthoebolaviruses are known to have caused illness in humans: Ebola virus, Sudan virus, Taï Forest virus and Bundibugyo virus. No human infections have been recorded from the two others which have also been identified, the Reston virus has caused disease in non-human primates; and Bombali virus which has been detected in bats. For a long time, these habitat suitability models have been the gold standard in this field of research. But the 2026 outbreak of the Bundibugyo virus in the Ituri province in the north-eastern region of the DRC has given us some pause. This is largely because of the conditions under which the outbreak emerged. The region is known for frequent conflict and food insecurity, with large displacement of people looking to escape the conflict, who then increasingly fall back on subsistence rainforest-related and mining activities. Typically, anthropogenic factors, i.e. driven by human activities, aren’t of great interest in HSMs. In Moir’s modelling studies at the CERI, however, they were curious to see if a model that also incorporates the effect of human activities on spillover events could better predict orthoebolavirus spillovers. In short, they set out to build a broader model. First, they mapped where possible animal reservoir species and orthoebolaviruses were most likely to occur. Moir’s team then also built a model for the distribution of orthoebolaviruses, which combined these maps with data on mining, human settlement, forest loss, bushmeat exposure and conflict. The aim was to identify places where ecological suitability and opportunities for human exposure overlap. Where people and wildlife meet A reservoir is an animal species in which a pathogen can persist, often without making the animal ill. The natural reservoir of orthoebolaviruses has never been confirmed. For their analysis, the researchers focused on three fruit bat species that have been proposed as possible reservoirs: the hammer-headed bat (Hypsignathus monstrosus), Franquet’s epauletted fruit bat (Epomops franqueti) and the little collared fruit bat (Myonycteris torquata). The evidence needs to be interpreted carefully. No infectious orthoebolavirus has yet been isolated directly from a bat.3 The possible role of bats is based largely on the detection of antibodies or fragments of viral genetic material, together with epidemiological investigations of human infections. The researchers therefore treated the bats as putative, not confirmed reservoirs. Using previously published models of bat and virus distributions, the team identified areas with high ecological suitability. They then examined where these areas coincided with human activities and pressures that could increase contact between people and possible animal hosts. Eastern DRC illustrates how those factors may converge. Conflict and displacement can push communities towards artisanal mining, hunting and other forest-dependent livelihoods. Mining and expanding settlements can disturb forests, while the loss of established livelihoods may increase reliance on bushmeat. Together, these changes can create more opportunities for contact between people and wildlife. Communities in the region have also faced outbreaks of Clade 1b mpox and cholera, adding to an already complex public health setting. The researchers describe this convergence as a syndemic environment. Medical anthropologist Merrill Singer developed the concept to explain how diseases interact with social and structural conditions, particularly among poor and underserved populations. In this study, the term is used more broadly to describe the overlapping ecological, social and economic pressures that can help create spillover hotspots. Putting the model to the test The researchers assessed how well different models matched the locations of previous Ebola spillover events. They used the Boyce index, a statistical measure designed for models built on recorded occurrences. Put simply, it tests whether observed events are concentrated in areas that a model predicts to be more suitable. The closer the match, the better the model performs. Models that combined viral habitat suitability with human influences, including the built environment, bushmeat exposure and forest loss, performed significantly better than those based on habitat suitability alone. The results suggest that ecological suitability provides the underlying landscape in which spillover potential can occur, but does not fully explain where recent events have been concentrated. Human activities alter that landscape and affect the likelihood that people and possible animal hosts will come into contact. Mining, expanding human settlements, forest disturbance, wildlife exploitation and exposure to conflict emerged as important predictors of a spillover. The model cannot predict that an outbreak will occur in a particular place or at a particular time. Nor can it establish which animal species transmit orthoebolaviruses to people. Instead, it identifies places where several conditions associated with spillover coincide, and where closer surveillance may be valuable. From risk maps to preparedness For public health agencies, a useful risk map needs to do more than indicate where a virus might circulate. It should identify the interfaces between people, animals and changing environments where surveillance and limited resources could have the greatest effect. By incorporating ecological suitability and human activity, the model could produce more accurate and operationally relevant risk maps. These could help direct surveillance efforts and resources towards the human–environment interfaces where spillover is most likely to occur. They may also inform surveillance strategies that account for the human activities and pressures shaping pathogen emergence in different landscapes.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the factors contributing to orthoebolavirus spillover events, particularly focusing on the Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the DRC in 2026. The researchers developed a model that integrates ecological and anthropogenic factors to predict where spillovers may occur, highlighting the role of human activity in increasing risk. The model suggests that conditions such as conflict, food insecurity, and displacement bring communities closer to wildlife, thereby raising the likelihood of spillover. These findings offer a more nuanced understanding of spillover risks than traditional habitat suitability models, which only consider environmental factors. The study's implications for public health include the need to incorporate human behavior into surveillance and risk assessment strategies. However, the evidence is limited to a single outbreak, which may restrict the generalizability of the results. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to these limitations.

papers.title: NEXTEBOVAX: ONTCIJFERING VAN ORTHOEBOLAVIRUS-IMMUNITEIT Mechanismen van homologe en heterologe bescherming tegen orthoebolavirussen in preklinische modellen
papers.abstract: The family Filoviridae consists of antigenically distinct human pathogenic viruses such as, among others, Ebola virus, Marburg virus and Sudan virus. Filoviruses have evolved sophisticated ways of evading the immune response thereby causing high mortality rates, and outbreaks are recurring over the past decades. Only two vaccines have been granted market authorization by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) for Ebola virus, yet none for the other highly pathogenic filoviruses. The aim of this PhD thesis is to study the protective efficacy of transgenic yellow fever 17D vectored vaccine candidates targeting the glycoprotein of the distinct filoviruses in small animal models, and with sera derived from small animal models. To that end, we will make use of pseudotyped filoviruses, such as recombinant vesicular stomatitis viruses carrying the glycoprotein of these filoviruses, which can be used within biosafety level 2 facilities, as well as a wide range of assays to evaluate the immune response elicited by the experimental vaccine candidates to ultimately determine the quality of the protective efficacy of these vaccine candidates.​

papers.title: Pathways to health resilience: A cross-country analysis of health system response to re-emerging infectious diseases in Sub-Saharan Africa.
papers.abstract: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) faces recurrent threats from re-emerging infectious diseases, including Ebola virus disease, cholera, measles, Lassa fever, and Marburg virus disease. This study assessed the resilience of health systems in 25 SSA countries from 2000 to 2023 using a multidimensional resilience index and a first-order Markov state-transition framework. Country-year observations were classified as Low Resilience, Moderate Resilience, or High Resilience based on epidemiological performance, health financing, surveillance, response capacity, and recovery indicators. Resilience was heterogeneous and path-dependent. Low-Resilience observations had an 82.4% probability of remaining in that state in the subsequent year and only a 3.1% probability of moving directly to High Resilience. Moderate-Resilience observations had a 19.1% probability of transitioning to High Resilience and an 18.2% probability of declining to Low Resilience. High-Resilience observations had a 63.6% probability of remaining High Resilience, but a combined 36.4% probability of regression. Multinomial logistic regression showed that health expenditure per capita, domestic health-financing share, and GDP per capita were positively associated with High Resilience, whereas internal armed conflict was negatively associated with High Resilience. Southern and Eastern Africa showed stronger resilience profiles than Western and Central Africa, while Central Africa had the greatest concentration of Low-Resilience countries. These findings indicate that resilience is dynamic, unevenly distributed, and strongly shaped by sustained financing, economic capacity, and political stability. Policy priorities include strengthening domestic health financing, targeting Moderate-Resilience countries for accelerated improvement, supporting conflict-affected systems, and harmonising regional surveillance and emergency-response mechanisms.

papers.title_zh: 健康韧性路径:撒哈拉以南非洲国家应对重新出现的传染病的卫生系统响应跨国家分析。
papers.source_body_en: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) faces recurrent threats from re-emerging infectious diseases, including Ebola virus disease, cholera, measles, Lassa fever, and Marburg virus disease. This study assessed the resilience of health systems in 25 SSA countries from 2000 to 2023 using a multidimensional resilience index and a first-order Markov state-transition framework. Country-year observations were classified as Low Resilience, Moderate Resilience, or High Resilience based on epidemiological performance, health financing, surveillance, response capacity, and recovery indicators. Resilience was heterogeneous and path-dependent. Low-Resilience observations had an 82.4% probability of remaining in that state in the subsequent year and only a 3.1% probability of moving directly to High Resilience. Moderate-Resilience observations had a 19.1% probability of transitioning to High Resilience and an 18.2% probability of declining to Low Resilience. High-Resilience observations had a 63.6% probability of remaining High Resilience, but a combined 36.4% probability of regression. Multinomial logistic regression showed that health expenditure per capita, domestic health-financing share, and GDP per capita were positively associated with High Resilience, whereas internal armed conflict was negatively associated with High Resilience. Southern and Eastern Africa showed stronger resilience profiles than Western and Central Africa, while Central Africa had the greatest concentration of Low-Resilience countries. These findings indicate that resilience is dynamic, unevenly distributed, and strongly shaped by sustained financing, economic capacity, and political stability. Policy priorities include strengthening domestic health financing, targeting Moderate-Resilience countries for accelerated improvement, supporting conflict-affected systems, and harmonising regional surveillance and emergency-response mechanisms.
papers.abstract_zh: 撒哈拉以南非洲(SSA)面临重新出现的传染病的反复威胁,包括埃博拉病毒病、霍乱、麻疹、拉沙热和马尔堡病毒病。本研究使用多维韧性指数和一阶马尔可夫状态转移框架,评估了2000年至2023年间撒哈拉以南非洲25个国家卫生系统的韧性。国家-年份观察结果根据流行病学表现、卫生筹资、监测、响应能力及恢复指标被分类为低韧性、中等韧性或高韧性。韧性表现出异质性和路径依赖性。低韧性观察结果在下一年保持低韧性的概率为82.4%,直接转移到高韧性的概率仅为3.1%。中等韧性观察结果有19.1%的概率转移到高韧性,有18.2%的概率下降到低韧性。高韧性观察结果有63.6%的概率保持高韧性,但有36.4%的综合概率出现倒退。多分类逻辑回归分析表明,人均卫生支出、国内卫生筹资占比和人均GDP与高韧性呈正相关,而内部武装冲突则与高韧性呈负相关。南部和东部非洲表现出更强的韧性特征,而西部和中部非洲的韧性较弱,中部非洲则拥有最多的低韧性国家。这些发现表明,韧性是动态的、分布不均的,并且受到持续筹资、经济能力和政治稳定等因素的强烈影响。政策优先事项包括加强国内卫生筹资、针对中等韧性国家加速改善、支持受冲突影响的卫生系统,以及协调区域监测和应急响应机制。

papers.title: Clinical and Operational Implementation of Ansuvimab under Expanded Access for Ebola Patients in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) is a zoonosis caused by Orthoebolavirus zairense (EBOV). Outbreaks of EVD have occurred in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), and an Expanded Access Program (EAP) with ansuvimab was implemented. OBJECTIVES: The primary objectives were to treat individuals with EBOV infection and to provide post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to those with high-risk exposure. STUDY DESIGN: We reported a descriptive expanded-access case series from the 11th, 12th, and 13th EVD outbreaks in the DRC. Following each outbreak declaration, the ansuvimab EAP protocol was updated and approved by the ethics committee. Eligible participants received ansuvimab intravenously. RESULTS: Twenty-four participants with confirmed EBOV infection and three PEP participants received ansuvimab during the 11th, 12th, and 13th EVD outbreaks. Most treated participants received ansuvimab within 7 days of symptom onset. Three of 24 EBOV-infected participants died; all three had baseline high viral load. No PEP participant developed EVD. No serious adverse events or new safety signals were identified CONCLUSIONS: Rapid protocol adaptation, ethics review, and in-country product storage enabled ansuvimab delivery during EVD outbreaks. Favorable clinical outcomes were consistent with previous findings, although small sample size, lack of a comparator, and predominance of participants with lower viral load limited interpretation.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:埃博拉病毒病(埃博拉病毒病,EVD)是由刚果盆地埃博拉病毒(Orthoebolavirus zairense,EBOV)引起的疾病。在刚果民主共和国(DRC)发生了第11次、第12次和第13次埃博拉病毒病暴发,并实施了安苏维单抗(ansuvimab)的扩展访问计划(Expanded Access Program,EAP)。目标:主要目标是治疗埃博拉病毒(EBOV)感染个体,并为高风险暴露者提供暴露后预防(post-exposure prophylaxis,PEP)。研究设计:我们报告了来自刚果民主共和国第11次、第12次和第13次埃博拉病毒病暴发的描述性扩展访问病例系列。每次暴发声明后,安苏维单抗扩展访问计划(EAP)协议都会更新并由伦理委员会批准。符合条件的参与者通过静脉注射接受安苏维单抗。结果:在第11次、第12次和第13次埃博拉病毒病暴发期间,共有24名确诊埃博拉病毒(EBOV)感染的参与者和3名暴露后预防(PEP)参与者接受了安苏维单抗治疗。大多数接受治疗的参与者在发病后7天内接受了安苏维单抗。24名埃博拉病毒(EBOV)感染者中有3人死亡,而这3人都具有基线高病毒载量。没有暴露后预防(PEP)参与者发展为埃博拉病毒病(EVD)。未发现严重不良事件或新的安全信号。结论:快速的协议调整、伦理审查以及在国内的药品储存使安苏维单抗能够在埃博拉病毒病(EVD)暴发期间及时交付。有利的临床结果与先前发现一致,尽管样本量较小、缺乏对照组以及大多数参与者具有较低病毒载量限制了结果的解释。

papers.title: Notes from the Field: The First 100 Days of Five Ebola Outbreaks - Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and West Africa, 2007-2026.
papers.abstract: The first 100 days after identification of an outbreak are important to understanding transmission dynamics, impact of early public health interventions, and trajectory of potential future cases and deaths. A large Ebola disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), which has become the country's largest and deadliest, is ongoing. To better understand the current outbreak, this report compared metrics from the first 100 days of this outbreak with those of four past Ebola outbreaks. The historic outbreaks of Ebola disease selected for this comparison include the two largest (the 2014 outbreak in West Africa and a 2018 outbreak in DRC), and the only two previous outbreaks caused by Bundibugyo virus (the 2007 outbreak in Uganda and the 2012 outbreak in DRC). This activity was reviewed by CDC, deemed not research, and conducted consistent with applicable federal law and CDC policy.

papers.source_body_en: The first 100 days after identification of an outbreak are important to understanding transmission dynamics, impact of early public health interventions, and trajectory of potential future cases and deaths. A large Ebola disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), which has become the country's largest and deadliest, is ongoing. To better understand the current outbreak, this report compared metrics from the first 100 days of this outbreak with those of four past Ebola outbreaks. The historic outbreaks of Ebola disease selected for this comparison include the two largest (the 2014 outbreak in West Africa and a 2018 outbreak in DRC), and the only two previous outbreaks caused by Bundibugyo virus (the 2007 outbreak in Uganda and the 2012 outbreak in DRC). This activity was reviewed by CDC, deemed not research, and conducted consistent with applicable federal law and CDC policy.

papers.full_text: The seventeenth Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) presents a paradox: we are better at detecting transmission than at stopping it. It is caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), for which no licensed vaccine or therapeutic exists. As of 11 August 2026, the national response had reported 4,566 confirmed cases and 2,128 confirmed deaths, corresponding to a case/fatality ratio of 46.6%. During the preceding 24 h alone, 118 new confirmed cases and 67 deaths were reported — the highest daily number of confirmed cases recorded during the outbreak1. This trajectory continues despite substantial surveillance. Of 324 suspected cases validated during the reporting period, 99.7% were investigated, while 17,085 out of 20,728 contacts were followed, giving a national follow-up coverage of 82.4%. These figures demonstrate operational capacity, but they also expose a fundamental limitation of conventional outbreak dashboards: coverage is not the same as effectiveness. The proportion of alerts investigated, or contacts followed, describes the reach of surveillance; it does not establish whether surveillance was sufficiently timely to prevent secondary transmission1. This distinction matters for BDBV. Unlike Zaire ebolavirus, for which licensed vaccines and therapeutics exist, no vaccine or specific therapeutic is available for BDBV. Consequently, rapid detection, isolation, infection prevention and control, supportive care and community engagement remain central to outbreak control2,3,4. The humanitarian and health-system context of this outbreak pose additional challenges2,3. The crucial unit of performance should be the interval between detection and intervention. Surveillance is valuable only if alerts can be rapidly translated into investigation, laboratory confirmation, isolation, appropriate care, contact tracing, and sustained follow-up. These steps form a temporal chain in which delay at any point creates opportunities for onward transmission. Evidence from previous Ebola outbreaks supports this interpretation: delayed isolation has been associated with community transmission, while modeling studies indicate that shortening time to isolation can substantially reduce epidemic size, even when diagnostic sensitivity is not optimal5,6. The DRC outbreak provides an unusually clear signal of this problem. Ituri accounted for 3,912 of the 4,566 confirmed cases and 98 of the 118 new cases reported during the preceding 24 h. Of its 36 health zones, 28 were affected. At the same time, the response reported important constraints: two ambulances were out of service in Ituri, seven health zones in North Kivu had no ambulance coverage, four health zones lacked a treatment or isolation center, and several treatment centers were saturated. These constraints create a pathway through which a detected infection may remain transmissible in the community1. Community mortality may be the clearest indicator of this response gap. Of the 67 confirmed deaths reported during the latest 24-h period, 50 occurred in the community and 17 in treatment centers. Community deaths should not be interpreted simply as a downstream measure of disease severity. In an Ebola outbreak, they can also signal that the response pathway failed to reach an infectious individual before death. They may reflect delays in symptom recognition, care seeking, referral, transport, diagnosis or isolation, as well as incomplete contact tracing, inadequate access to care, insecurity or community resistance1. This interpretation is supported by experience from previous Ebola responses. During the 2018–2020 DRC outbreak, delays in isolation and community deaths were recognized as mechanisms that could amplify transmission. In Uganda’s 2022 Sudan virus disease outbreak, 43% of confirmed patients entered effective isolation at least 6 days after symptom onset, with lack of transport and fear of Ebola treatment units as contributors to delayed care7. The relevance of these findings to the present BDBV outbreak is not that the circumstances are identical, but that time outside effective isolation remains a modifiable determinant of both transmission and survival. A recent mathematical modeling study found that shortening time to isolation or increasing testing access could markedly reduce epidemic size, supporting the value of rapid diagnostic-to-isolation pathways6. Meanwhile, genomics has identified a previously unrecorded BDBV variant associated with the current outbreak, reinforcing the importance of combining genomic, epidemiological and operational intelligence rather than relying on case counts alone7. The implication is not that surveillance has failed. Instead, the outbreak suggests that surveillance performance and response performance are partially decoupled. This distinction affects how outbreak response is measured. We propose that Ebola response dashboards add a new response-effectiveness cascade to existing surveillance indicators, measuring, in real time: (i) time from alert to investigation; (ii) time from investigation to specimen collection; (iii) time from specimen collection to laboratory result; (iv) time from confirmation to effective isolation; (v) time from isolation to definitive supportive care; (vi) the proportion of contacts reached within the first follow-up interval; and (vii) the proportion of deaths occurring in the community before effective isolation (Table 1). These indicators would transform surveillance from a system that primarily describes where transmission is occurring into one that also identifies where intervention is failing to occur rapidly enough. Together, they shift the unit of performance from coverage to speed. Importantly, these measures should be disaggregated by health zone. The national contact-follow-up rate of 82.4% approaches the operational threshold of 85%, but this aggregate conceals major heterogeneity: coverage was only 60.7% in North Kivu. National averages can create a false impression of system-wide resilience. The response system is only as strong as its least responsive transmission corridor1. This perspective also reframes community deaths. Instead of treating them solely as an endpoint, response teams could interpret the proportion of deaths that occur outside treatment centers as a sentinel indicator of missed opportunities for intervention. A sudden increase in community deaths should trigger an operational investigation: where were these patients first symptomatic? Were they previously listed as contacts? How long did they remain in the community after symptom onset? Was transport available? Was testing accessible? How long did confirmation take? Were treatment and isolation facilities functioning? Were social, security or trust-related barriers involved? Such questions would connect epidemiological surveillance to the operational reality of outbreak response. They would also complement recent efforts to develop real-time epidemic intelligence for the BDBV outbreak3, with the objective of identifying the bottleneck(s) at which information fails to become action. The central lesson is broader than Ebola. Detection is an information outcome; interruption is a public-health outcome. They should not be measured as if they were equivalent. In an outbreak in which therapeutic and vaccine options remain limited, the interval between these two outcomes will largely determine transmission and mortality. For DRC, and future outbreaks, the ultimate test of surveillance should not be the number of alerts investigated or contacts followed. The ultimate measure of surveillance is how many cases, and deaths, we prevent.
